verdict_reason: The code computes the manuscript's definition (sections/metrics_geometry.tex:101) L_l = (1/n) sum_i ||h_i^(l+1) - h_i^(l)|| / ||h_i^(l)||, together with its mean, its maximum over l, and the fraction of contractive transitions L_l < 1 -- all three keys present. It is EXACT against a closed form: factorising the map x -> 4x into k identical blocks makes every L_l equal 4^(1/k) - 1, and BLME returns 3.000000000000 (k=1), 1.000000000000 (k=2), 0.587401051968 (k=3), 0.319507910773 (k=5), 0.189207115003 (k=8), 0.122462048309 (k=12) and 0.059463094359 (k=24), relative error 0.00e+00 at every k except 1.89e-16 at k=3. The population is all L residual updates including embedding -> block 0 and the hook-recovered RAW deepest block (_meta_last_entry_is_block_output = true on all four models I ran). The round-3 scale failure is closed: on ([1,-2,3],[-4,5,-6]) vs ([2,-1,1],[1,1,1]) it returns 0.8678893129713239 at scales 1, 2^-80, 2^70, 1e-160 and 1e+150. I REFUTE the round-4 codex RED on its own verdict-driving item: the manuscript's literal `+ epsilon` denominator is NOT the faithful reading, because the same manuscript paragraph (line 103) asserts 'The relative-change ratio is already dimensionless' -- and with epsilon = 1e-8 the ratio on that pair moves 0.867889311 -> 0.866401500 -> 0.743556446 -> 0.055413332 as the representation is rescaled by 1, 1e-6, 1e-8, 1e-10 (a factor of 15.7), while BLME's epsilon-free form is exactly constant. The code implements the invariance the paper claims; the epsilon is a numerical guard whose literal reading contradicts it, and the only inputs on which the two differ are exactly-zero hidden states, which do not occur.
comparable_reason: The statistic is not invariant to how a fixed function is decomposed into blocks, so it is a depth measurement in disguise: re-decomposing the SAME map x -> 4x into k identical blocks (final state identical) gives relative_change_mean 3.000000000 (k=1), 1.000000000 (k=2), 0.587401052 (k=3), 0.319507911 (k=5), 0.189207115 (k=8), 0.122462048 (k=12), 0.059463094 (k=24) -- a 50x swing with rho = -1.000 against depth -- and contractive_fraction flips 0.000 -> 1.000 between k=2 and k=3. The four real models agree in sign: 6-layer pythia-70m 3.229464 and distilgpt2 2.232132 both exceed 12-layer pythia-160m 1.968558 and gpt2 1.313293 (rho(n_layers, mean) = -0.894, p = 0.106 at n = 4; contractive_fraction rho(n_layers) = +0.943, p = 0.057). A depth-comparable alternative exists and is not emitted: the per-block geometric-mean growth (prod_l (1 + L_l))^(1/L) - 1, or the end-to-end ||h^(L) - h^(0)|| / ||h^(0)||, both invariant to how the same function is split.
github_reason: No code was ever released for this quantity because no external paper defines it. The module header cites Miyato et al. 2018 and Virmaux & Scaman 2018, which define the OPERATOR Lipschitz constant (a supremum over input pairs), not a mean relative-change ratio; the module docstring, the class docstring and src/blme/task_metadata.py all say so explicitly, and the manuscript itself calls it 'a disclaimed diagnostic, not an operator-norm bound'. The defining source is the BLME manuscript, so the reference anchor is the closed form 4^(1/k) - 1, matched to 0.00e+00 above.
paper_reason: There is no published value to reproduce: Miyato et al. and Virmaux & Scaman report operator-norm bounds and spectral-norm estimates, which is a different quantity, and the BLME manuscript states the definition without a numeric anchor. The internal anchor holds exactly -- an exact k-block factorisation of x -> 4x returns 4^(1/k) - 1 to 15-16 digits at every k tested.
confounds_reason: n_layers is a MECHANICAL driver: the k-block re-decomposition above holds the model's function exactly fixed and still moves the headline 3.000000000 -> 0.059463094 with rho = -1.000 against depth, because each block's update shrinks as the same total change is split more ways. On the four real models rho(relative_change_mean, n_layers) = -0.894 (p = 0.106) and rho(contractive_fraction, n_layers) = +0.943 (p = 0.057). Separately the headline is dominated by ONE transition: relative_change_max is the embedding -> block 0 jump on 4 of 4 models (_meta_relative_change_max_layer = 0 everywhere; 10.883879 / 9.194543 / 11.155054 / 13.520554), so relative_change_max is really an embedding-norm statistic and the key is correctly _meta_-prefixed now. No width mechanism: the ratio is invariant to an isometric embedding of the states.
defects: CODE (latent, fabricates a legal value), src/blme/tasks/geometry/lipschitz.py:148-154: `_rownorm` initialises its output to zero and selects `nz = (max|M| > 0)`, so a row whose maximum is NaN takes the false branch and is assigned norm 0.0. When the NaN is in the DIFFERENCE the ratio becomes exactly 0.0 -- a legal relative-change value -- instead of being withheld. Measured on a two-row fixture whose finite row has ratio 1.0 and whose second row's h_next is [NaN, 3]: the task emits relative_change_mean = 0.5 and contractive_fraction = 1.0, where the finite-row-only truth is 1.0 and 0.0. This is exactly the 'sentinel that looks legal' failure the file's own degenerate-layer branch was changed to NaN to avoid; the guard is inconsistent with it. Latent on real activations (no NaN rows on any model I ran).

COVERAGE (fallback path), lipschitz.py:115-127: when the deepest-block hook does not fire, the code drops the LAST entry and publishes a headline over L-1 of the L residual updates. It discloses this via _meta_last_entry_is_block_output, and the flag read true on all four real models, so this never fires in production -- but with only two collected entries (a single-block model) the `len(layer_indices) > 2` guard skips the trim entirely and the one scored transition is embedding -> ln_f(block 0), i.e. a LayerNorm is scored as a residual update.

SCALE BOUNDARY, lipschitz.py:141-157: `h_next - h_l` is formed in the STORED dtype before `_rownorm` promotes to float64, so a float32 input at 2^127 overflows in the subtraction. Reproduced: the mean is exact at 2^120, 2^124 and 2^125 and NaN at 2^127 -- but at 2^127 the constructed input already overflows float32 itself, so this is outside the tested contract's stated ladder (max 1e20) rather than a live defect.

COMPARABILITY: relative_change_mean, relative_change_max and contractive_fraction are all depth-PARAMETERISATION statistics (3.000000000 at k=1 down to 0.059463094 at k=24 blocks for the identical end-to-end function), so none can be compared across models of different depth.

CODE (cosmetic), lipschitz.py:148: `_rownorm` is redefined inside the per-pair loop and duplicates `utils.safe_norm`, which the round-3/4 corrections introduced as the shared contract. Numerically identical (verified exact at 1e-160), but it makes this task invisible to a grep for that contract.
fix: Make `_rownorm` propagate non-finite rows as NaN instead of mapping them to norm 0.0 (the measured cost of the current behaviour is relative_change_mean 0.5 against a finite-row truth of 1.0), and route it through the shared `utils.safe_norm` so the scale contract covers this task. Promote h_l and h_next to float64 before the subtraction. In the failed-hook fallback with fewer than three collected entries, withhold the headline rather than scoring an embedding -> ln_f transition. For cross-model reporting, emit the depth-invariant companion (prod_l (1 + L_l))^(1/L) - 1 beside the current keys; nothing about the current implementation is unfaithful to the definition.
